title: Silent Launch: Adaptive Quantization comms playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick scratch playbook for a silent (limited-traffic) rollout of 'Adaptive Quantization' on Hosted API. This is a working note — rough phrasing, likely Qs, escalation paths, and sample Slack/email copy. NOT the final customer announce.

High-level intent (one line): ship perf/cost win to 5% of traffic quietly to validate metrics and rollback safety before broader rollout.

Quick wins we expect: ~20-35% token-cost reduction on avg for Llama-family variants on p4, latency change +/- 5ms median (should be neutral), tail latency unaffected in canary region.

Rollout plan (technical):
- Phase A: 1% traffic, single region (us-west2). Duration: 48h monitoring window.
- Phase B: 5% traffic, two regions (us-west2, eu-west1). Duration: 72h.
- Phase C: Expand to 25% if no regressions and quality gating passed.
- Auto-rollback triggers: >2% drop in exact-match for eval prompts, >5% increase in 95th percentile latency, customer error-rate bump >0.2% absolute.

Monitoring signals to watch (primary):
- Token cost per request (billing-derived instrument)
- Generation quality baseline delta (eval-suite rolling comparison)
- 95p and 99p latency per model family
- Error rates and model fallbacks (increased fallback would be red)
- Customer-reported anomalies via support channel

Owner & escalation:
- Launch owner: Camila Ortiz (product-hosted-api) — primary on-call for rollout decisions first 72h.
- SRE on-call: Pager team (channel: #sre-oncall)
- Model QA: Noelle Park (applied-ml) — quality gate signoff
- Exec contact: Jonas Meyer (VP Product) — for any customer-impacting incident

Internal comms cadence (what to tell internal teams):
- Day -1 (preflight): short note in #product-hosted-api and #sre-ops with links to dashboards + timeframe.
- Day 0 (kickoff): slack ping to a small group (#alpha-rollouts) with baseline metrics snapshot + canary target list.
- Every 12h during Phases A/B: quick status blip in #alpha-rollouts (1–2 bullets).
- On green-to-expand decision: notify sales/CS leads and AMA channel with customer-facing embargo guidance.

Sample internal slack: (short, to #alpha-rollouts)

Soon: starting silent canary for Adaptive Quantization (AQ) — 1% traffic into us-west2 for 48h. Owner: Camila O. Primary signals: token-cost, 95p latency, eval-delta. Watch dashboards: <link>. If you see anything odd, ping @camila and #sre-oncall immediately.

(continue)

Suggested quick FAQ / crib answers (for internal spokespeople):
Q: What is Adaptive Quantization?
A: It’s a runtime optimization that reduces per-token compute precision where safe, delivering lower inference cost while preserving output quality on common workloads.

Q: Will this change model outputs?
A: For the vast majority of requests we do not expect any measurable drift. We run an automated eval set and human spot-checks as part of the rollout. Any unexpected regressions trigger rollback.

Q: Is any customer data used to tune this?
A: No customer data is used to train models or tune quantization heuristics. All validation runs are on synthetic and anonymized internal eval sets.

Q: Can customers opt-out?
A: In this silent canary phase, traffic is selected server-side for validation; we will add an opt-out route for customers in the beta if/when we expand. For Dedicated/private deployments there is no automatic change.

Q: Could this affect latency?
A: It may slightly change median latency (mostly neutral), but we are monitoring tail latencies carefully. Any negative tail impact will be blocked.

Do-not-say / risky framing:
- Don’t use the word "precision loss" or suggest we are "downgrading model quality."
- Avoid promising specific % cost savings to customers until Phase B metrics are stable.
- Don’t imply this is a replacement for model improvements — it is an inference optimization.

Customer-facing embargo language (short paragraph for CS/Sales to prep; do not publish):
We’re running a controlled validation of an inference optimization designed to lower per-token cost and improve efficiency for certain model families. During this limited validation we do not expect customer-visible changes; if we see anything unexpected we’ll revert immediately. We’ll share results and next steps after the evaluation window.

Sample short internal all-hands talking point (30s):
We’re quietly experimenting with an inference optimization called adaptive quantization that lets us serve models more cheaply without retraining. We’re running a small validation to measure cost and quality — if results are strong, this will be a behind-the-scenes lever to improve unit economics for customers.

Open questions / TODOs (scratch):
- Confirm exact eval prompt set and acceptance thresholds with Noelle by EOD today.
- Wire up billing-metric to the rollout dashboard (INF-2219).
- Draft customer opt-out API flag if we hit Phase B.
- Prep short KB article if we expand beyond 5%.
- Confirm legal/privacy signoff for communication (is any phrasing needed about data use?).

Quick contingency scripts (ops):
- If eval delta crosses threshold: automated rollback trigger + immediate message to #alpha-rollouts with rollback reason and timestamp.
- If support spikes: temp open a triage bridge (#alpha-rollouts + #support) and escalate to Jonas + SRE manager.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep internal messages concise; don't over-explain the tech in initial pings.
- Save broader metrics summary for Phase B decision memo.
- Check with CS leads whether they want a proactive heads-up to top-20 customers.

References:
- Eval dashboard: <internal-link>/dashboards/adaptive-quant-eval
- JIRA: INF-2219 (rollout wiring)
